column1: Atomic Audit|1998|10|10|1996|9,9,8,8,8,9,8,9,7,8|Stephen I. Schwartz (editor)|Reconstructs nuclear weapons costs across production, deployment, command, disposal and oversight. The publisher contents support a system-wide accounting investigation rather than a technical reference manual. Financial and organizational constraints transfer well, but US military policy dominates both thematic deductions. Evidence: https://www.brookings.edu/books/atomic-audit/ ; https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/1998/08/atomic-audit-table-of-contents.pdf

The Media Lab|1987|10|0|1987|6,8,7,6,7,7,9,8,8,7|Stewart Brand|Reports on an interdisciplinary computing research organization and its ambitions. Links between tools, funding and research culture fit the profile, while contemporary predictions require separation from demonstrated achievements. This source mentions a separate extended review; this assessment uses the identified subject and available bibliographic description, not a claimed full-text audit.

Cat Sense|2013|0|0||8,5,4,7,7,8,3,9,8,8|John Bradshaw|Explains domestic-cat behavior through evolution, development and human interaction. Mechanisms have comparative biological interest, but little direct strategic or industrial relevance. It is explanatory animal science rather than a veterinary procedural manual. Density remains a description-level estimate.

Urne Burial|1658|0|10||6,4,4,3,5,9,1,8,4,9|Thomas Browne|An antiquarian discovery prompts reflections on death, memory and impermanence. Its conceptual and literary payload passes V3, but difficult allusions reduce accessible learning and causal depth. The source stresses linguistic virtuosity rather than a reusable scientific model. Philosophy dominates; the meditations have no single historical endpoint.

The Dark Side of the Enlightenment: Wizards, Alchemists, and Spiritual Seekers in the Age of Reason|2013|0|0|1800|8,6,5,5,7,8,4,8,8,8|John V. Fleming|Examines intellectual practices that coexisted with Enlightenment rationalism. The source values the corrective to a simple progress narrative. Historical analysis of spiritual movements is not doctrinal advocacy; evidence and institutional context provide a modest transferable payload.

The Notenki Memoirs|2002|10|10|2002|7,6,5,5,6,7,4,8,7,6|Yasuhiro Takeda|First-person history of Gainax connects fan networks, creative production and business organization. The source reports useful production history but uneven attention to the best-known work. Media and Japanese institutional history dominate. Original Japanese publication predates the 2005 English edition.

The Genius Factory|2005|10|0|1999|8,7,6,6,7,8,4,8,8,7|David Plotz|Investigates donor selection, information asymmetry and commercialization at a US sperm bank. These institutional mechanisms are transferable even though the subject is peripheral. The source supplies a substantial reader account; it is a history of a eugenics project, not an endorsement of its aims.

Don’t Sleep, There Are Snakes|2008|0|0|2008|7,6,5,6,7,8,3,8,8,7|Daniel Everett|Combines fieldwork memoir with arguments about language and cultural constraints. Firsthand observations are valuable, but general claims about recursion require more than one field account. It is explanatory anthropology, not a language-training course; neither religious conversion nor its abandonment alone determines a veto.

A History of Life-Extensionism in the Twentieth Century|2014|10|0|2000|7,7,6,6,7,8,6,7,6,7|Ilia Stambler|Traces researchers and movements across several countries, connecting biological programs with institutions and social aims. The source reports broad coverage and many capsule histories; this supports substantial learning with some catalog-like stretches. Aging and health dominate T11, while the text remains historical rather than procedural medicine.

Moondust|2005|10|0|2005|7,5,4,4,4,7,6,6,7,6|Andrew Smith|Interviews with lunar astronauts examine life after Apollo. The source identifies interesting operational details but substantial author-centered interpretation and limited interview material. Spaceflight supplies domain relevance; US personal history and low-yield passages limit priority. The science/high-tech memoir exception prevents an automatic V3.

Bitcoin: The future of money?|2014|0|10|2014|6,7,6,6,6,6,6,6,8,7|Dominic Frisby|Explains the early cryptocurrency movement and its monetary claims. The source records participation in fact-checking but provides no full-book quality assessment here. Distinguish operational mechanisms from early adoption forecasts; finance is central and the historical snapshot ends around publication.

Playboy Interview II|1983|10|10|1982|7,6,5,4,8,7,2,7,8,7|Barry G. Golson (editor)|Long interviews provide varied perspectives and sustained questioning. The source reports unusual depth and preparation, supporting a high density estimate despite weak direct-domain fit. Celebrity, US culture and media remain central; general discussions offer enough conceptual content to avoid V3.

Spec Ops|1995|0|10|1976|8,7,8,8,8,9,6,9,8,8|William H. McRaven|Comparative operation histories develop a model of relative superiority, preparation, speed and surprise. Case comparisons provide constraints and failure modes rather than merely tactical instructions. Selection of exceptional missions limits generalization. The last central case is Entebbe in 1976; the 1993 thesis is treated as the same underlying work.

A Life of Sir Francis Galton|2001|0|0|1911|7,7,6,6,7,9,7,8,8,7|Nicholas Wright Gillham|Connects measurement, heredity, exploration and scientific institutions through Galton's career. The source finds the heredity disputes informative but criticizes incomplete statistical explanations. Science biography remains eligible; discussion of eugenics is historical, not automatically advocacy.

The Grand Strategy of the Roman Empire|1976|0|10|337|6,8,8,7,8,9,7,8,8,8|Edward N. Luttwak|Connects frontier geography, client states, force concentration and imperial costs. The source highlights useful strategic comparisons while questioning whether coherent-looking outcomes establish a centrally intended strategy. That inference risk lowers E and M; ancient subject age reaches the H13 cap.

The Grand Strategy of the Byzantine Empire|2009|0|10|1453|7,8,8,7,8,9,7,8,8,8|Edward N. Luttwak|Explains diplomacy, intelligence and selective force as responses to persistent strategic constraints. The source favors its neglected historical material, but this is not an independent audit of its controversial strategic synthesis. Military strategy is central; the broad Byzantine period ends in 1453.

The Vaccinators|2007|10|0|1868|9,8,7,8,8,9,6,9,8,8|Ann Jannetta|Explains how fragile biological material and medical knowledge crossed trade and institutional barriers. Networks, trust and transport constraints give the disease-centered history strong transferable value. Publisher description and the source review support eligibility as historical explanation. Evidence: https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvqsf11h

Life in Our Phage World|2014|10|0||8,7,6,8,8,8,6,9,8,7|Forest Rohwer, Merry Youle, Nao Hisakawa and Heather Maughan|Illustrated explanations of phage diversity develop evolutionary constraints, genetic compression and host-parasite feedback. Despite the field-guide subtitle, the source describes explanatory narratives and interviews rather than a laboratory or identification reference. Ecological interactions are central, so T11 applies. Evidence: https://books.google.com/books/about/Life_in_Our_Phage_World.html?id=g4HTrQEACAAJ

Tombstone|2008|10|10|1962|9,8,8,8,7,9,5,9,8,8|Yang Jisheng|Documents famine and the feedback between coercive targets, false reporting and institutional fear. These mechanisms strongly transfer beyond the Chinese case. The source describes accumulating evidence rather than mere repetitive assertion. Both single-nation tragedy and political power dominate; original Chinese publication is 2008, not the English edition's 2012.

Drugs 2.0|2013|0|0|2013|7,8,7,7,7,7,6,8,8,7|Mike Power|Connects chemical variation, online communities, regulation and distributed supply chains. The source reports substantial new knowledge about the development of research-chemical markets. This is journalism about innovation and markets, not drug synthesis or consumption instructions. A changing market snapshot limits durability.

The Hall of Uselessness|2011|0|0||8,5,5,4,7,8,2,9,8,9|Simon Leys|Collected literary and cultural essays supply distinctions about interpretation, authority and historical memory. The source identifies strong China essays but a largely literary focus. Miscellaneous structure limits systems integration without implying that each new case is padding.

The Psychology of Invention in the Mathematical Field|1945|0|0||7,6,8,6,8,9,9,10,7,8|Jacques Hadamard|Examines discovery through preparation, incubation, insight and checking, drawing on mathematicians' reports. Introspective evidence limits causal certainty, but differences in mental imagery and working habits provide durable intellectual tools. It explains discovery rather than teaching mathematical proofs, so it passes H3.

The Ideological Origins of the American Revolution|1967|10|10|1776|9,7,6,7,7,9,4,10,8,8|Bernard Bailyn|Uses pamphlets to explain how political ideas and perceived threats shaped revolutionary choices. The source wanted more primary quotation, but reports convincing documentary support. The work analyzes ideology rather than recruiting for a present movement; American political history incurs both thematic deductions.

The Operations Evaluation Group|1984|10|10|1980|8,9,9,8,6,9,9,8,7,8|Keith R. Tidman|Naval research history links measurement, search, equipment and institutional decisions. The source gives concrete examples of improved tactics but also substantial internal administration and omissions around strategic consequences. Eligibility rests on explanatory history, not formal operations-research training. US military focus receives both deductions. Evidence: https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Operations_Evaluation_Group.html?id=7TMgAAAAMAAJ
